questions.q: Under Defender XDR, what happens to Defender for Endpoint's core concepts like onboarding and AIR?
options: They stay the same — a device still has to be onboarded, and AIR still investigates and remediates the same way; what changes is where the telemetry goes next
AIR is replaced entirely by a manual-only review process under Defender XDR
Defender for Endpoint stops functioning once Defender XDR is turned on
Onboarding is no longer required once Defender XDR is enabled
questions.explain: Defender XDR doesn't change how Defender for Endpoint onboards devices or runs AIR — it changes the scope an alert gets evaluated against.

questions.q: What is the real difference in how an endpoint alert is evaluated under Defender XDR compared to before?
options: It's evaluated exclusively by a human analyst with no automation involved
It's evaluated only against alerts from the exact same device
It's evaluated against alerts from Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps too, not just other endpoint alerts
It's no longer evaluated at all once XDR is enabled
questions.explain: Defender XDR's unified incident engine checks an endpoint alert against signal from the other three workloads, which can reveal it's part of a larger incident.

questions.q: What does the Microsoft Sentinel data connector for Defender XDR actually bring into a Sentinel workspace?
options: A complete replacement of Sentinel's own analytics rules
Defender XDR's already-correlated incidents, plus raw Advanced Hunting tables like DeviceProcessEvents and AlertInfo
Only a static PDF report summarizing Defender XDR activity
Nothing — Defender XDR and Sentinel cannot be connected in any way
questions.explain: The connector ingests both Defender XDR's correlated incidents and the underlying Advanced Hunting schema tables into the Log Analytics workspace.

questions.q: Why would a SOC connect Defender XDR to Sentinel when Defender XDR already has its own unified portal?
options: Because Defender XDR's portal cannot display incidents without Sentinel installed
Because the connector is required before Defender for Endpoint can onboard any devices
Because Sentinel and Defender XDR show identical data with no benefit to combining them
Because Sentinel can see data Defender XDR never will, such as firewall, VPN, or non-Microsoft SaaS logs, enabling cross-source correlation
questions.explain: The value is scope — joining Defender XDR's tables against non-Microsoft data sources inside one KQL query is something neither tool does alone.

questions.q: Which of these is a real Advanced Hunting schema table name mentioned in this lesson?
options: DeviceLogonEvents
FirewallAccessLog
VpnSessionTable
EndpointAuditTrail
questions.explain: DeviceLogonEvents, along with DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceNetworkEvents, AlertInfo, and AlertEvidence, are real Advanced Hunting schema tables shared with Sentinel.
